latest_nl_proof:
Fix an integer m>=2 and a tuple x=(x_1,…,x_{m-1}) with each x_r>0. Define
S_x:=\{km:k\in \mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\}\cup \bigcup_{t=1}^{m-1}\{qm+t:q\in \mathbb Z_{\ge 0},\ q\ge x_t\}.
We must show that for each fixed r\in\{1,\dots,m-1\}, the least positive integer q such that qm+r\in S_x is exactly x_r.

So fix r\in\{1,\dots,m-1\}. First, since x_r is a positive integer, it is in particular a nonnegative integer and satisfies x_r\ge x_r. Therefore, by the defining clause of S_x corresponding to the same residue class r, the integer x_r m+r belongs to S_x. Hence the set
A_r:=\{q\in \mathbb Z_{>0}: qm+r\in S_x\}
is nonempty, and x_r\in A_r.

It remains to show that no positive integer q<x_r belongs to A_r. Let q\in \mathbb Z_{>0} and assume qm+r\in S_x. By the definition of S_x, membership can occur in one of the following ways.

1. It could be that qm+r is a nonnegative multiple of m, say qm+r=km for some k\in \mathbb Z_{\ge 0}. Then r=(k-q)m. But 1\le r\le m-1, while the right-hand side is divisible by m. This is impossible.

2. Otherwise, there exists some t\in\{1,\dots,m-1\} such that qm+r is in the t-th union component, so
qm+r=q' m+t
for some q'\in \mathbb Z_{\ge 0} with q'\ge x_t.
Rearranging gives
(q-q')m=t-r.
Now t-r satisfies -(m-2)\le t-r\le m-2, and in particular |t-r|<m. Since the left-hand side is divisible by m, t-r must also be divisible by m. The only multiple of m with absolute value strictly less than m is 0, so t-r=0. Hence t=r. Then (q-q')m=0, so q=q'. Because q'\ge x_r, we obtain q\ge x_r.

Thus every positive integer q with qm+r\in S_x satisfies q\ge x_r. Combined with the earlier observation that x_r m+r\in S_x, this shows that x_r is the smallest positive integer q for which qm+r\in S_x.

Since r was arbitrary, the conclusion holds for every r\in\{1,\dots,m-1\}. Therefore, for each such r, the least positive integer q with qm+r\in S_x is exactly x_r.
role_in_parent: Provides one side of the inverse relationship, namely Phi(Psi(x)) = x.
statement_nl: Fix an integer m >= 2 and a tuple x=(x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers. Define S_x to be the set consisting of all nonnegative multiples of m and, for each r in {1,...,m-1}, all integers q m + r where q is a nonnegative integer and q >= x_r. Then for each r in {1,...,m-1}, the least positive integer q such that q m + r belongs to S_x is exactly x_r.

domain_restrictions: m is an integer with m ≥ 2
x_r is a positive integer for each r ∈ {1,...,m-1}
r ranges over the finite set {1,2,...,m-1}
S_x includes all integers of the form k*m with k ∈ Z_{>=0} (so 0 is included in S_x)
For each r ∈ {1,...,m-1}, S_x additionally includes all integers of the form q*m + r with q ∈ Z_{>=0} and q ≥ x_r
In the conclusion, q is required to be a positive integer (q ∈ Z_{>0})
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For fixed m ≥ 2 and fixed tuple x=(x_1,...,x_{m-1}) with each x_r ∈ Z_{>0}, define S_x := {k*m : k ∈ Z_{>=0}} ∪ ⋃_{r=1}^{m-1} {q*m + r : q ∈ Z_{>=0}, q ≥ x_r}. Then for every r ∈ {1,...,m-1}: (i) x_r*m + r ∈ S_x, and (ii) for all q ∈ Z_{>0}, if q*m + r ∈ S_x then q ≥ x_r; hence the least positive integer q with q*m + r ∈ S_x is exactly x_r.
quantifier_order: Let q be the least element of { q ∈ Z_{>0} : q*m + r ∈ S_x }

variables.name: x
variables.role: fixed parameter vector x=(x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers

variables.domain: Z_{>0} (when minimized), and Z_{>=0} in the definition of S_x
variables.name: q
variables.role: multiplier used in the expression q*m + r; minimized in the claim

variables.name: S_x
variables.role: subset of integers defined in terms of m and x

witness_dependencies: The minimizing q depends on the chosen r (the claim is per-r) and on the parameters (m,x) via the condition q ≥ x_r in the definition of S_x
The value that q is asserted to equal, x_r, is the coordinate of the fixed tuple x corresponding to the same residue index r
